name: Sirenomelia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Sirenomelia

criteria.description: Fusion of the lower limbs resulting in a single lower limb structure
Bilateral renal agenesis or severe renal hypoplasia
Malformations of the external and internal genitalia
Presence of imperforate anus or other gastrointestinal anomalies
Presence of a single umbilical artery instead of two

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fused lower limbs and bilateral renal agenesis or severe renal hypoplasia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and supported by imaging studies.

laboratory: Oligohydramnios detected via amniotic fluid index
Abnormal renal function tests if kidneys partially functional
imaging: Ultrasound showing fused lower limbs and absent kidneys
MRI or fetal CT confirming limb fusion and visceral anomalies
X-ray demonstrating sacral agenesis and vertebral anomalies
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; mostly sporadic cases
Possible association with maternal diabetes mellitus
other: Single umbilical artery on placental examination

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of two separate lower limbs
Complete absence of one or more limbs rather than fusion

redFlags: Respiratory distress due to pulmonary hypoplasia
Incompatible with life in most cases due to renal failure
references: Sirenomelia: Clinical and Radiological Features. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 2019.
Mermaid Syndrome: A Review of Pathogenesis and Clinical Presentation. Pediatric Surgery International, 2021.
Prenatal Diagnosis and Management of Sirenomelia. Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology, 2020.
